thesis: MasTec is a top-tier North American specialty infrastructure contractor levered to grid modernization, natural gas pipelines, renewables and — increasingly — inside-the-fence electrical work for AI data centers via the $1.65B Superior Group acquisition closed in July 2026. Q2 2026 set records: revenue $4.37B (+23% YoY), adjusted EBITDA $384M (+40%), adjusted EPS $2.22 (+49%), and an 18-month backlog of $21.4B (+30% YoY) on 1.2x book-to-bill. Management raised FY2026 guidance to $18.2B revenue, $1.6B adjusted EBITDA and $9.30 adjusted EPS, yet the stock has fallen ~54% from its 52-week high of $441 to $204 on a cut to the Communications outlook and a sector-wide AI-capex sentiment shock in September 2026. At 18.8x forward earnings, ~12x FY2026E EV/EBITDA and a PEG of 0.47 against a record backlog, the risk/reward has flipped in the buyer's favour — the main caveats are 2.2x pro-forma net leverage, thin trailing free cash flow of $245M, and the unresolved question of how much data-center work actually gets awarded.

financials.fcf: $245M TTM; >$1B operating cash flow guided for FY2026, Q4-weighted

drivers: Mission-critical/data-center awards convert: management is pursuing several large turnkey and hyperscaler-connectivity packages expected to be awarded by year-end 2026 and to revenue in 2027
Superior Group ($1.65B, ~3,000 electricians, ~$1.4B 18-month backlog) lifts Power Delivery margins into the low double digits and opens cross-selling across the platform
FY2027 EPS reaches consensus ~$12.4 and the multiple re-rates back toward peer levels, closing the gap to the $414 average analyst target
Communications recovers in 2027 as new spectrum equipment ships and deferred wireline starts unlock
Pipeline Infrastructure sustains ~18% EBITDA margins with backlog at its highest level since 2020

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 lands on guidance ($18.2B revenue, $1.6B adjusted EBITDA, $9.30 adjusted EPS) and Q4 delivers the bulk of the >$1B operating cash flow, taking net leverage below 2.0x. FY2027 revenue grows in the mid-to-high teens on the $21.4B backlog plus Superior, EPS reaches $11.50–12.40, and the stock trades at 22–24x forward earnings (~10x EV/EBITDA) — a discount to its own history that reflects lingering AI-capex uncertainty.

risks: AI data-center capex digests: cancelled or paused projects and state-level moratoria push clean-energy and power-delivery awards into 2028, and backlog growth stalls
Communications weakness persists past 2026 — FY2026 segment revenue already cut to ~$3.25B with margins ~100bps lower YoY
Fixed-price execution misses repeat; the Q2 flow-through shortfall on fuel, equipment and project execution proves structural rather than timing
The Q4-weighted >$1B operating cash flow target is missed, leaving net leverage above 2.0x after the $1.65B Superior deal
Multiple compresses to 7–8x EV/EBITDA, the level cyclical E&C names trade at in a capex downturn

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings (after close). Company guide: revenue $4.9B, adjusted EBITDA $482M, adjusted EPS $2.98. First reported Superior Group backlog and the Communications margin step-up of ~200bps versus the first half are the swing factors.

Majority of the guided >$1B FY2026 operating cash flow is expected to land, with net leverage targeted below 2.0x by year-end. Management also expects additional large mission-critical and turnkey data-center awards before year-end.
FY2026 results and initial FY2027 guidance — the first hard read on whether the $21.4B+ backlog converts and whether Communications inflects.
New spectrum equipment becomes available to carriers, the stated trigger for the deferred wireless build cycle that hit the 2026 Communications outlook.

key_risks: AI/data-center capex sentiment: September 2026 brought an industry-wide AI-slowdown scare plus reports of cancelled and paused data-center projects, which can defer the awards underpinning the growth case
Communications segment: FY2026 revenue cut by ~$400M to ~$3.25B on wireless spectrum equipment delays and wireline project deferrals; Q2 segment EBITDA margin fell 170bps YoY to 8.2%
Leverage and integration: $3.24B total debt, ~$2.9B net debt, net leverage 1.8x reported and 2.2x pro forma for Superior — the largest acquisition in company history
Cash conversion: TTM free cash flow of only $245M on $16.1B of revenue; the >$1B operating cash flow guide is heavily back-half weighted and working capital has consumed the earnings growth so far
Fixed-price contract execution: unapproved change orders sat just above $200M at Q2, and one poor large project can absorb a quarter of segment profit
Beta of 1.82 and 6.8% of shares short mean the equity trades as a high-torque proxy for infrastructure and AI-capex sentiment rather than on fundamentals
